description: Smart Wi-Fi Plug with Power Monitoring & Matter
config_flow_sub_profile_remarks:
You need to select a profile depending on your settings.
The ECO setting only changes the power consumption in the listed configurations. Activating any other settings not listed in the profile name will change the power draw.

Note: The Wi-Fi repeater function was disabled during all measurements.

LED status indicator variants (PLUGS_UI `leds.mode`):
- "LED": `leds.mode = "switch"`, i.e. the LED follows the output state, not the measured power. `colors.switch:0.on` = rgb [0, 100, 0] at brightness 100, `colors.switch:0.off` = brightness 0 (LED dark). Night mode disabled.
- "No LED": `leds.mode = "off"`, LED indication disabled completely. The `power` mode was not used for any measurement.

Sub-profile configurations:
"WLAN + BT + ECO": All three turned on.
"WLAN + ECO": Both turned on.
"WLAN + BT": Both turned on, ECO turned off.
"WLAN": Only WLAN turned on, ECO turned off.
measure_description:
Setup: the tested plug and a calibrated resistive dummy load are connected in parallel to the same mains input, and a second Shelly Plug S Gen3 measures upstream of both. The dummy load is never connected to the relay output, so the reference meter always reads about 33 W and can resolve the sub-watt self-consumption of the plug. The plug stays powered in both relay states; only the output relay changes, so the meter always sees the plug plus the dummy load.

The dummy load was calibrated with the measurement tool at 1600.01 Ohm, i.e. about 33 W at 230 V. Its contribution is subtracted from every sample instead of being applied as a fixed offset, because it follows the mains voltage:

    P_self = P_upstream - (V^2 / R)

The tool applies this per sample and averages over the measurement window for each state. Two plateaus from the reference meter log during the run, one with the relay off and one with it on:

- Relay OFF: V = 229.9 V, P_upstream = 33.70 W, V^2/R = 33.03 W, resulting P_self = 0.67 W.
- Relay ON (no load at the output): V = 230.0 V, P_upstream = 34.10 W, V^2/R = 33.06 W, resulting P_self = 1.04 W.

The stored sub-profile values are the averages of these per-sample subtractions over the whole window, so a single plateau can differ from the stored value by a few tenths of a watt. For sub-profiles with LED enabled, the LED was active at full brightness only while the relay was switched on. Firmware version 2.1.1.
